correctness.rationale: For omitted A-vertices, outer distance multisets are determined by the suffix count of B-landmarks; omitted B-vertices are controlled symmetrically by A-prefix counts. Injectivity yields |W| at least n-1. Equality makes every possible count occur exactly once, and paired prefix/suffix inequalities force x_1=0, y_n=0, and x_{k+1}+y_k=1. The converse formulas show that these shifted-pair choices resolve precisely unless the two side landmark counts are equal. The packaged exhaustive checker confirms all bases through n=10.

value.rationale: The theorem completely resolves a natural distance-identification invariant on the canonical twin-free chain family, including every minimum set. The odd-order balanced obstruction and the even-order complete shifted-pair family reveal a meaningful parity phenomenon caused specifically by discarding landmark identities.
